key_insight: CSF adds scene awareness to text-conditioned motion generation by filtering motions based on context, not just the prompt. This helps the same action be judged differently depending on what or ով it targets in the scene.
problem_solved: Text-to-motion systems can generate physically trackable motion, but they lack scene-dependent safety understanding. Existing defenses mainly inspect prompts, rely on labeled motion datasets, or enforce geometry-only rules, so they miss how context changes whether a motion is safe or unsafe.
method: Training-free contextual safety filtering applied after or during motion generation.
Grounds natural-language safety rules in scene context to evaluate whether a motion is safe in the current environment.
Distinguishes between similar motions with different targets or meanings based on surrounding objects and people.
impact: This makes motion generation safer and more deployable in real-world settings where context determines risk. For practitioners, it offers a practical way to reduce harmful outputs without retraining large motion models or collecting new labeled safety data.
visual_elements: A split-scene illustration showing the same motion becoming safe or unsafe depending on the target object/person.

paper_title: CSF: Contextual Safety Filtering for Motion Generators
paper_authors: Lizhi Yang, Yiling Hou, Yao Tang, Junheng Li, Daniel Weng
